1	# Fields: purpose, acquisition, and rendering
2	
3	This document specifies the card, not a new agent planning system. References
4	such as S1 point to [verified source findings](source-findings.md).
5	
6	## Scope and truthfulness
7	
8	Use the current plate as the initial implementation scope for applied settings
9	and estimates. Show its name beside the estimate, or beside the summary if no
10	estimate exists. Clicking an object must not silently change this scope.
11	This is a proposed implementation default to prevent mixing a project-wide
12	setting statement with a single-plate estimate. Include only printable copies
13	on that plate when deciding whether values are uniform (S5).
14	
15	The intent belongs to the chat. Inactive cards use the saved plate scope,
16	intent, settings summary, details, estimates, and validity from that chat's
17	checkpoint. Selecting a plate on today's canvas must not rewrite them.
18	Snapshot structured values and the summary's interpretation/version together
19	through the lifecycle mechanism; do not reconstruct using today's presets.
20	
21	Read native facts through a coherent snapshot on the GUI thread. The page
22	formats and selects facts; it does not merge raw Orca configurations or issue
23	agent tool calls to refresh its own display. Bind delayed updates to the
24	project/chat/checkpoint and discard results for a replaced scope.
25	
26	## Card state model
27	
28	Figma section ⑥ shows combinations of independent facts, not eight unrelated
29	card implementations. Keep these axes separate in the read model:
30	
31	- conversation ownership: active/current or earlier/saved;
32	- setup source: agent-managed setup or selected-preset fallback;
33	- activity: stable, agent working, or a completed change that can be undone;
34	- estimate validity: current, recomputing, stale, or unavailable;
35	- last authoritative editor when known: agent or user; and
36	- deterministic attention findings.
37	
38	Render the following reviewed examples from those facts:
39	
40	| Figma state | Required meaning |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| Just changed | A completed, attributable settings transition. Show concise before/after values only when both snapshots cover the same scope. Undo must call the normal Orca undo path; never maintain a card-only reverse patch. |
43	| Agent working | Keep showing the last confirmed setup and estimates. Progress copy must not expose speculative settings as applied. |
44	| Estimate recomputing | Settings are confirmed, but time and material are pending. Preserve previous figures only when they are explicitly labeled non-current. |
45	| Out of date | The displayed previous estimate or saved setup no longer matches its live comparison scope. Explain the invalidating change and offer an existing refresh/recompute path. |
46	| Edited by hand | A reliable native change source attributes the live settings change to the user. Preserve the settings; do not silently ask the agent to reapply its version. If authorship is not reliable, omit the label. |
47	| One-line risk | One deterministic, actionable finding. Omit the row when the check is not applicable or its inputs are unknown. |
48	| No agent configured | Show the selected preset as a neutral fallback. Do not imply that an agent reviewed or optimized it. |
49	| Sliced and sent | A saved snapshot associated with a slice/send event. Keep pre-slice estimates distinct from measured print results; show actuals as unavailable unless a physical-print record supplies them. |
50	
51	Conversation status outranks live activity: an earlier/saved card never becomes
52	`Agent working` because the current chat is busy. Setup source and estimate
53	validity remain visible where relevant. Attention is conditional content, not a
54	success/failure state for the whole card.
55	
56	## 1. Intent title
57	
58	**Why:** explain the purpose of this setup in the user's terms. It is the only
59	semantic summary authored from conversation in this card.
60	
61	**Existing source:** `ProjectStateDocument::setup_intent(conversation_id)` is
62	already chat-specific. Currently it is populated from the optional `intent`
63	argument of a successful `settings_apply_patch`, so it is not a complete intent
64	capture lifecycle (S1). `IntentField` also exists, but its arbitrary field/value
65	text should not become a new intent/strategy/plan hierarchy in the UI.
66	
67	**Required change:** keep one saved title per chat; allow its writer to update
68	when an explicit user request establishes or changes intent, including a turn
69	without a settings mutation. Reuse the existing store field where practical.
70	Determine the narrow bridge/agent-recording path during implementation; no
71	general summary endpoint is claimed to exist. The agent may condense user text
72	but must not derive purpose from infill or a preset name. On ambiguity, retain
73	the last explicit intent or use a neutral `Setup summary` title, rather than
74	inventing `Strong part` or treating an agent suggestion as user intent.
75	
76	Manual setting edits update settings, not intent. Renaming a conversation need
77	not rewrite intent. Keep text wrapping sensible at 320 DIP; do not use the
78	current 40-character tool-argument limit as permission to truncate meaning.
79	Preserve established project requirements outside this title. This is not a
80	request to remove the project's intent records or silently reset them.
81	
82	## 2. Applied-settings summary
83	
84	**Why:** reveal the most consequential configuration at a glance, without
85	requiring the user to interpret a full parameter diff.
86	
87	**Derivation in two sentences:** Format layer height, wall loops, infill, and
88	support mode from the resolved settings for printable content on the chosen
89	plate, including unchanged inherited values. Detect special modes and local
90	variation before emitting a uniform value; use scoped exceptions or explicit
91	`varies`/`local settings` wording when a compact exact summary is not justified.
92	
93	No agent reasoning is required. Use stable config keys, not English UI labels
94	or substrings of preset names. Existing process/object reads are a starting
95	point, not proof of complete resolution (S2–S5).
96	
97	| Fact | Candidate native keys/data | Display rule |
98	| --- | --- | --- |
99	| Layer height | `layer_height`; plate/object overrides; `ModelObject::layer_height_profile`, layer ranges | Show a single normal layer height only when uniform. Identify variable layer height when present. Show a numeric range only if obtained from authoritative resolved data; never infer it from the nominal preset value. |
100	| Walls | `wall_loops`, object/part/modifier/range configs | Show configured wall loops. Say `4 walls; tabs use 6` only when those regions and effective values are verified. Do not imply the toolpath has exactly that count everywhere or that load capacity is validated. |
101	| Infill | `sparse_infill_density`, `sparse_infill_pattern`, local overrides | At 0%, say `No sparse infill`; omit an irrelevant pattern. At 100%, report `100% infill` without claiming the selected sparse pattern describes solid toolpaths. Otherwise show density and human-readable enum label. |
102	| Supports | `enable_support`, `support_type`, `support_on_build_plate_only`; blockers/enforcers/paint | Describe configured mode, e.g. `Tree supports · build plate only`. `Off throughout` requires verifying relevant scope, not just the global flag. Paint/modifiers should be disclosed when consequential. Enabled support settings do not prove supports will actually be generated. |
103	| Special mode | `spiral_mode`; `PartPlate::get_spiral_vase_mode()` resolves plate/global flag | Use `Spiral vase mode` rather than an ordinary walls/infill sentence that may contradict mode behavior. Do not invent a physical wall count. |
104	
105	Typical order: layer height and walls on the first line; infill and supports on
106	the second. This is a content budget, not a clipping rule. Wrap at narrow widths.
107	Put a short, consequential local exception in these lines; put the full list
108	in details. Do not order the summary by which parameter happened to change last.
109	
110	### Coverage before precision
111	
112	Do not create a parallel slicer configuration engine in React. Inspect Orca's
113	existing resolution path (S3), reuse native read mechanisms where their contract
114	is adequate, and expose a fork-owned read model. A renderer needs, for each
115	summary fact, its scope, value/enum/unit, and whether coverage is complete,
116	mixed, or unavailable. Exact field names are implementation choices.
117	
118	The existing reader only overlays object config on a preset. Before making a
119	plate-wide claim, cover plate overrides, model parts, modifier volumes,
120	height-range overrides, variable-height profiles, and nonprinting copies.
121	If a supported simple case has no relevant exceptions, emit exact values.
122	If values genuinely vary and all applicable values are known, show `2–6 wall
123	loops` or a short scoped exception. If complex/overlapping modifiers cannot be
124	resolved reliably before slicing, say `Local wall settings — see details` and
125	list the configured overrides with their targets. Do not present a configured
126	modifier's value as proven coverage of a physical region.
127	
128	A named `Mounting tabs` exception requires a valid region binding and current
129	modifier values. A stored region record, volume name, or artifact existence
130	alone is insufficient (S6). Imported/manual modifiers must not disappear just
131	because no agent region record exists. Use actual object/volume names when
132	semantic labels are unavailable. Exclude unsupported printer technologies
133	from FFF-specific claims; use explicit unavailability instead of empty success.
134	
135	## 3. Time and material
136	
137	**Why:** expose the expected cost in machine time and filament. Both numbers
138	belong to the same plate and slice result.
139	
140	**Source:** `WorkspacePlate::estimate`, `estimate_status`, `sliced`, and
141	`invalidated_by`, already bridged to the page (S7). Use native estimates;
142	never ask the model to guess time or grams from geometry or infill.
143	
144	Use the same row/component in current and historical cards:
145	`clock icon  ~42 min    material icon  18 g    Plate 1`.
146	Use the existing rounding helpers where suitable; verify hour formatting
147	against Figma's `~2h 18m` example. Do not use color or a checkmark to imply print
148	readiness.
149	
150	Currency is optional content, not a required field in this iteration. Figma
151	section ⑦ includes a currency value only to prove the facts row can accept one
152	without changing its anatomy. Show cost only when an authoritative native
153	calculation supplies its value, currency, and matching plate/slice scope. Do
154	not reserve an empty slot, derive a cost in React, or add a currency setting to
155	implement the stress-test fixture.
156	
157	| Estimate state | Behavior |
158	| --- | --- |
159	| Current | Normal numbers and plate scope. |
160	| Never sliced / no usable estimate | No fake zeros. Show `Not sliced yet · estimates unavailable` only when native state establishes that; otherwise `Estimate unavailable`. A visible `Compute estimates` action must use the existing slice/estimate path. |
161	| Stale | Preserve prior numbers when available and label them `Previous estimates · not current`. Offer `Refresh setup & recompute` only when that action can re-read settings and start the authoritative estimate path. Never compare stale figures against a requirement as if current. |
162	| Recomputing | Say `Time & material estimates recomputing…`. Preserve prior numbers only when separately labeled non-current; replace time and material together when the result is current. |
163	| Historical | Same row and formatting, with historical status on the whole card. Retain the estimate's validity when saved. Today's slicing must not replace its numbers. |
164	
165	Restoration does not automatically validate a historical slice. Follow Orca's
166	actual validity result. The reviewed design therefore treats restored estimates
167	as unverified until native state confirms them. Numeric zero and missing data
168	are not interchangeable; the
169	native estimate may hold only a usable time or usable mass, so verify how the
170	read model represents each unavailable measure before formatting it (S7).
171	
172	## 4. Needs attention
173	
174	**Why:** reserve prominence for a concrete, actionable inconsistency.
175	
176	Keep deterministic findings only. There is no reliable generic unresolved-
177	question relevance tracker already available for this UI. Do not infer one
178	from unanswered conversation text, `PlanRecord.risks`, or model confidence.
179	
180	Begin with existing configured-versus-reported/confirmed printer mismatches
181	and native validation findings that the implementation can expose without
182	duplicating checks (S8). Do not imply all print risks have been checked.
183	No findings means omit the block, not display `Safe to print`.
184	
185	Figma shows configured PETG versus reported PLA. The existing comparison
186	checks whether a configured material appears anywhere in the reported loaded
187	material list; it does not establish slot-to-filament assignment. Match that
188	scope in the copy. Do not claim `slot 1 is wrong` or `PETG is loaded` based on
189	the current check alone. Show the report's actual timestamp when available;
190	Figma's `1 min ago` is invented example data, not an implemented freshness
191	guarantee. Unknown, missing, offline, or stale observations cannot be a passed
192	check. Determine how the printer owner exposes freshness; if it cannot prove
193	currency, label `Last reported material differs` with the timestamp instead
194	of a present-tense hardware assertion. Do not invent a silent TTL.
195	
196	Recompute/clear findings on settings, printer selection, connection/telemetry,
197	and confirmed-fact changes/expiry, even without a new chat turn. Derive findings
198	from current inputs; do not maintain a second list of manually resolved alerts.
199	Historical cards retain findings as of the saved checkpoint; live preflight
200	and printer status remain outside that historical snapshot.
201	
202	An action must open the relevant existing control or explain the compared
203	values; it must not silently alter hardware or settings. `Review material` in
204	the mockup only reveals the compared facts. If several checks fail, use stable
205	priority and expose the count/details rather than hiding additional blockers.
206	
207	**Excluded from this iteration:** parse arbitrary intent prose into time,
208	weight, or strength requirements. `IntentChecks.hpp` uses permissive textual
209	heuristics (S9); this is not sufficient proof of a correctly scoped constraint.
210	Do not ship a `within your target` badge on that basis. Adding typed confirmed
211	limits is separate work, not necessary for this card. The intent title may
212	still quote `under 1 hour` without claiming an automated requirement check.
213	
214	## 5. Expanded details
215	
216	**Why:** make the compact summary inspectable without filling its default view
217	with low-priority values. These are selected configuration details, not a claim
218	to list every Orca parameter.
219	
220	Use the same sections in active and saved cards:
221	
222	1. **Printer & material:** selected printer, nozzle, filament assignments, and
223	   configured build plate. Use native configured setup (S8); show multiple
224	   assignments when present. Do not use `WorkspaceContext.printer.filament`
225	   alone for multi-material projects; it currently names only the first slot.
226	   The configured plate is not proof of which plate is physically installed.
227	2. **Applied settings · scope:** normal layer height, wall loops, sparse infill,
228	   top/bottom shell layer settings, support mode, and brim. All are effective
229	   values, including unchanged inherited values. Zero/off, mixed, and unknown
230	   need distinct rendering. Include top/bottom minimum thickness constraints
231	   when relevant; nominal layer counts alone may not describe resulting shells.
232	3. **Local overrides:** object/part/region/range target plus its actual override.
233	   `Support blockers applied` means verified configuration artifacts exist,
234	   not proof that a sliced hole will contain no support. Do not show `None`
235	   until inspection covers all supported local customization paths.
236	4. **Base preset and preset differences:** stable reference and a separate
237	   disclosure. Existing `presetDeltas` describes process-preset differences
238	   only (S10); label other scopes separately. A displayed change count must
239	   count the same rows the disclosure exposes. Grouped support/brim prose may
240	   represent multiple raw config keys, so use `Preset differences` without a
241	   numeric total when the count cannot be defended.
242	
243	Additional verified key names in `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp` are
244	`top_shell_layers`, `bottom_shell_layers`, `top_shell_thickness`,
245	`bottom_shell_thickness`, `brim_type`, `brim_width`, `nozzle_diameter`,
246	`filament_type`, and `curr_bed_type`. Existence of a key does not establish
247	its scope or inheritance; use the corresponding owner/read path.
248	
249	No separate Why/Strategy/Plan/Assumptions section. Detailed settings controls
250	and the existing transcript retain their jobs; this task does not introduce
251	a duplicate full parameter editor or a second manufacturing history.
252	
253	## 6. Earlier-chat project-update boundary
254	
255	Figma section ⑤ specifies a boundary below the saved transcript, not another
256	setup-card state. Render it only while an inactive project chat is viewed.
257	
258	- Changed: show **There have been project updates.** and explain that the
259	  chat's saved project must be restored to continue.
260	- Provide **Restore and resume**, **Return to active chat**, and **Ask current
261	  chat about this** with the lifecycle semantics in
262	  `context/chat-state-and-restoration.md`.
263	- Keep the continuation input locked with **Restore this chat to continue**.
264	  A disabled-looking control is insufficient; native command handling must
265	  also reject inactive sends, retries, approvals, and continuations.
266	- Do not place this block inside the setup card. It belongs at the end of the
267	  saved conversation and remains visible with the locked continuation state.
268	- For unchanged or unavailable checkpoints, use the corresponding truthful
269	  lifecycle copy and action availability. Do not claim project updates merely
270	  because a chat is inactive.
271	
272	The ordinary active-chat composer, chat title bar, and surrounding message
273	layout in the original references are outside this handoff. Only the historical
274	continuation lock and the project-update actions are in scope.

1	# JusPrin design system
2	
3	**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-newui`.
4	
5	JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.
6	
7	The original JusPrin logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints were verified from the source SVG. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.
8	
9	## Brand behavior
10	
11	- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
12	- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
13	- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
14	- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
15	- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.
16	
17	The logo suggests an end-to-end journey through its orbit, precision and momentum through the crossing diagonals, flexible control through the open circle, and technical confidence softened by warmth through the purple gradient.
18	
19	Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.
20	
21	## Logo use
22	
23	The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.
24	
25	- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
26	- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
27	- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
28	- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
29	- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
30	- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.
31	
32	Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.
33	
34	## Brand palette
35	
36	| Name | Value | Use |
37	|---|---:|---|
38	| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
39	| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
40	| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
41	| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
42	| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
43	| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
44	| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
45	| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
46	| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
47	| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |
48	
49	The signature gradient runs from Orbit to Bloom. Reserve it for the original logo, splash, onboarding, and rare hero moments. Do not use it as ordinary product chrome.
50	
51	Product code must resolve colors through semantic tokens in `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; raw palette values are not a component API.
52	
53	## Semantic color behavior
54	
55	Dark mode is a semantic remapping, not a visual inversion. Preserve hierarchy, density, and geometry while choosing the dark value for the same named intent.
56	
57	Core mappings include:
58	
59	| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
60	|---|---:|---:|---|
61	| `surface.canvas` | `#FFFFFF` | `#17131F` | Main application background |
62	| `surface.subtle` | `#F6F2F7` | `#211B2A` | Sidebars and grouped settings |
63	| `surface.raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#2B2336` | Dialogs, menus, elevated panels |
64	| `text.primary` | `#17131F` | `#F6F2F7` | Headings, values, body copy |
65	| `text.secondary` | `#5F5767` | `#CFC5D3` | Descriptions and secondary labels |
66	| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
67	| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
68	| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
69	| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
70	| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |
71	
72	The JSON token file is authoritative and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values.
73	
74	## Typography
75	
76	Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:
77	
78	- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
79	- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
80	- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
81	- The system GUI font as fallback.
82	- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.
83	
84	HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
85	and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
86	not need the monospace one. The native shell has no monospace text.
87	
88	Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.
89	
90	| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
91	|---|---:|---|
92	| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
93	| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
94	| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
95	| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
96	| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
97	| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
98	| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
99	| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
100	| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
101	| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |
102	| Code (system monospace) | 12/16 | Regular |
103	
104	The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
105	action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
106	its detail). Code is a single role, `typography.code`, whatever size the
107	text around it is.
108	
109	## Layout and geometry
110	
111	Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.
112	
113	- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP.
114	- Standard control radius: 4 DIP, matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
115	- Compact or branded action radius: 8 DIP.
116	- Container radius: 8 DIP, for grouped panels and cards, matching OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default.
117	- Window action and large-dialog radius: 12 DIP.
118	- Capsule radius: `pill`, for status chips and progress tracks whose shape is
119	  the full height. Menu rows sit inset 4 DIP inside the popover and carry the
120	  standard radius, so a hovered row reads as a control inside the panel
121	  rather than a stripe across it.
122	- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.
123	
124	Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.
125	
126	## Components and states
127	
128	Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in Figma, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.
129	
130	- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
131	- Shared progress track: 4 DIP from `component.progress.height`; PrinterCard and Agent activity use this role rather than owning separate track heights.
132	- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
133	- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
134	- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
135	- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
136	- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
137	- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
138	- Icon button: 26×26 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius.
139	- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
140	- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the Figma frames on the Plates & Project Pane page.
141	- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
142	- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
143	- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
144	- Agent-pane collapse: a 26 DIP icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.
145	
146	Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.
147	
148	## Accessibility
149	
150	- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
151	- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
152	- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
153	- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
154	- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
155	- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
156	- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.
157	
158	## Writing UI code
159	
160	Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
161	exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
162	the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
163	only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
164	
165	1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
166	   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
167	   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
168	   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
169	   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
170	   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
171	   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
172	   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
173	   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
174	2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
175	   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
176	   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
177	   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
178	   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
179	   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
180	   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
181	3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
182	   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
183	   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
184	4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
185	   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
186	   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
187	5. **Read the code on `jusprin-newui`, not old commit messages or Figma,
188	   when they disagree.** The header's chip and menu dimensions were once
189	   changed to match Figma and reverted because they looked worse; the
190	   token file records what stayed.
191	6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
192	   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
193	   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
194	   not that the result looks right.
195	7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
196	   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
197	   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
198	   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.
199	
200	## Runtime application in the native app
201	
202	The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
203	three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
204	color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
205	three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.
206	
207	1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
208	   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
209	   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
210	     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
211	     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
212	     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
213	     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
214	     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
215	     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
216	     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
217	     fonts.
218	   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
219	     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
220	     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
221	     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
222	     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
223	     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
224	     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
225	   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
226	     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
227	     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
228	     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
229	     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
230	     translucent rounded rectangles.
231	2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
232	   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
233	   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
234	   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
235	   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
236	     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
237	     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
238	     switches at once.
239	   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
240	     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
241	     color.
242	   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
243	     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
244	     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
245	     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
246	     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
247	     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
248	     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
249	   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
250	     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
251	     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
252	   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
253	     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
254	   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
255	     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
256	     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
257	     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
258	3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
259	   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
260	     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
261	     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
262	     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
263	   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
264	     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
265	     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
266	     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
267	     in About are excluded by the script.
268	   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
269	     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
270	     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
271	     reference it.
272	
273	`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
274	contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
275	the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
276	`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
277	the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
278	12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
279	button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.
280	
281	Known gaps, all deliberate: ImGui panels and canvas notifications keep the
282	teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
283	Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
284	links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
285	generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
286	were not visually verified.
287	
288	## Design handoff requirements
289	
290	Every high-fidelity product frame must:
291	
292	1. Define each application screen in one canonical appearance mode. Do not
293	   create paired light and dark screen frames. The other mode must be
294	   deterministically derived by the design system from the same semantic token
295	   names, component variants, geometry, content, and interaction state. Verify
296	   light/dark differences in the design-system primitives and semantic mappings
297	   rather than duplicating every application screen.
298	2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
299	3. Use DIP, native density, and the standard radius scale.
300	4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (Figma's Code style uses Roboto Mono as a stand-in for the system font).
301	5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
302	6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
303	7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
304	8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.
305	
306	The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify the checked-in functional icons against an unpacked lucide-static release.

Usage: python3 verify_lucide.py /path/to/unpacked/lucide-static/package
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    package = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
    manifest = json.loads((here / "lucide-map.json").read_text())
    package_manifest = json.loads((package / "package.json").read_text())
    expected = f"{manifest['package']}@{manifest['version']}"
    actual = f"{package_manifest['name']}@{package_manifest['version']}"
    if actual != expected:
        print(f"Expected {expected}, got {actual}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    mismatches = []
    known = set(manifest["icons"]) | {"agent-bot"}
    for extra in sorted({path.stem for path in here.glob("*.svg")} - known):
        mismatches.append(f"{extra}.svg has no provenance mapping")
    for local, upstream in manifest["icons"].items():
        if (here / f"{local}.svg").read_bytes() != (package / "icons" / f"{upstream}.svg").read_bytes():
            mismatches.append(f"{local}.svg != {upstream}.svg")
    if (here / "LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt").read_bytes() != (package / "LICENSE").read_bytes():
        mismatches.append("LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt != LICENSE")
    if mismatches:
        print("\n".join(mismatches), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"Verified {len(manifest['icons'])} SVGs and license against {expected}")
    return 0

**Update 2026-10-06: a fully deterministic, read-only way to read frames.** Kenneth's instruction that day: Figma is a read-only resource for the agent; never edit, rename or move anything (see [[figma-is-read-only]]). Dev Mode needs a seat upgrade ("Get Dev Mode") — decline it.

- **Node ids:** every layer row carries `data-testid="<nodeId>-layers-panel-row"`. Expand a section by dispatching pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click on its `[data-testid="layers-panel-expand-caret"]`, then read all rows.
- **Zoom/pan without the keyboard** (key presses do not reach the canvas): dispatch `WheelEvent('wheel', {ctrlKey:true, deltaY:+40, clientX, clientY})` on the `<canvas>`; each step zooms in ×1.18 anchored at the point (negative zooms out). Zoom menu → "Zoom to fit" gives a known start (26% on the Current Setup Card page). To put fit-view point C at screen point S with k = 1.18^n: anchor A = (k·C − S)/(k − 1). Screenshot coords × (innerWidth/800) = client coords. Wheel panning is unreliable; use the anchor formula and zoom back out at the same anchor.
- **Exact CSS + text per frame:** dispatch a `contextmenu` (button 2) on the row's inner element at a fixed clientX/Y, synthetic-hover "Copy/Paste as" → "Copy as code" (find by exact text), then a *real* tool click on "CSS (all layers)" (a synthetic click cannot copy). Patch `navigator.clipboard.writeText` in the page to capture the text into a window variable; `clipboard.readText` is denied. Layers that were never renamed carry their text as the layer name.
- The side panels hide with the "Minimize UI" button at the top of the left panel; they return on every page load.
EOF

## What was wrong and what changed

- **Card UI**: the half-done card didn't follow the Figma anatomy, so I rebuilt it in [SetupCard.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx) from the exact Figma layout values.
- **Old card removed**: the interim `AppliedSetupCard` and the old delta-only card are gone, because the host now always sends applied settings and they were unreachable.
- **Project-updates boundary**: [App.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx) now renders it once at the end of an earlier chat, with the three actions and the locked field.
- **Native read model**: brim settings were missing; I added them, plus the plate's default value and per-object grouping, which the three-object frames need.
- **Variable layer height**: a height range that only changed walls was being reported as "variable layer height"; fixed.
- **Icons**: six Lucide icons added from the pinned `lucide-static@1.47.0` (integrity hash matches the icons README).
- **Undo**: a new `undo_setup_change` shell action calls Orca's own undo. It is not exercised against the real app — only the page side (button and message) is tested.

## Tests and inspection

- **Visual cases**: one state input per Figma frame, plus a review page of the production card in light/dark at 405 and 320 DIP (sent to you above).
- **Visual inspection**: I checked every frame at 405 light against Figma and spot-checked 320 and dark. Sixteen of 19 card heights match Figma to the pixel, and nothing overflows at 320.
- **Agent page**: 315 tests pass, including one acceptance test per frame and tests for the handoff's behaviour call-outs.
- **Native unit suites**: all pass (`agent_bridge_tests` 286 cases, `jusprin_tests`, `workspace_contract_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, `brand_tokens_tests`).
- **Real Orca adapter harness**: 14 setup checks pass, including a modifier case where the old object read answers 5 walls for the whole plate and the new read reports it as local.
- **Real app**: `--recomputing-capture` and `--chat-restoration-capture` pass, including the native refusal of a send forged from an earlier chat.

Testing caught three bugs, all fixed and covered:
- A saved card could show the live "Agent working" block.
- After "Restore and resume" the card claimed "Edited by you", because the restore's own setting replay is logged under the person.
- A never-sliced plate read "unavailable for these edits".

## Where the card differs from the Figma samples

- **"Out of date" label**: the frame says "Earlier setup"; a live card keeps "Setup summary", since the settings shown are live and only the estimate is stale.
- **Material mismatch**: reads "Last reported material differs… Printer last reported PLA" with the report time, because the check can't prove what is loaded now.
- **Named exceptions**: "4 walls; Mounting tabs: 6" uses the modifier's real name and configured value. With several modifiers it says "Local wall settings — see details".
- **Three objects**: "Plate default: 0.20 mm layers · 4 walls", so no object's value reads as universal.
- **Undo**: only appears when the agent's last change is a project step on Orca's undo stack. Process-preset edits aren't on that stack, so they show the before/after with no Undo.
- **Three frames are 2 px taller than Figma**: Figma drew 14 px glyphs, but the guarded icon scale is 16/20/24, so I used 16.

## Not covered

- Real printer telemetry and the fake-Bambu path.
- macOS and Linux.
- "Another plate is slicing" and partial estimates (missing density) are tested on the page only, not against native state.
- The one-line risk row can render, but no native check produces a single-line finding yet; only printer mismatches feed attention today.
- The default full shell-harness mode; I ran only the two modes that touch the card.

- **Undo for preset-level changes**: leave it absent, or route it through the existing "Revert to here" version restore with its confirmation?

# JusPrin Figma Agent Design

Use Figma Agent to produce coherent, reviewable JusPrin product design while keeping the Figma file maintainable. Treat the user's request as the source of scope and use attached wireframes, screenshots, documents, and existing frames as design input.

## Ground the work in JusPrin

Before designing a surface that is intended for implementation:

1. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and the relevant product documents it points to.
2. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`. Treat `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` as the authoritative token source when Figma and the repository disagree.
3. Identify whether the surface belongs to the native wxWidgets shell, the embedded Agent page, or OrcaSlicer-owned UI. Respect the ownership boundaries in `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.
4. Design for a dense native desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux using DIP, including narrow-window and high-DPI behavior.

Use the current approved JusPrin Figma file and frames named by the user. Do not infer the approved source from canvas proximity, page order, or a numbered suffix. Older explorations and POC frames are reference material, not automatic sources of truth.

## Establish the starting point

Before prompting Figma Agent:

1. Identify the target Figma file, page, approved source frame, and existing states that must remain unchanged.
2. Inspect the relevant design-system page, variables, styles, and generic primitives. Search for the needed primitives before proposing new ones. Map them to the semantic roles in `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`.
3. Determine which starting mode applies:
   - **Wireframe-led:** preserve the wireframe's information architecture, content, behavior, and state distinctions. Add visual fidelity without silently redesigning the product concept.
   - **Existing-design revision:** preserve accepted structure and change only the requested areas.
   - **Exploratory:** when no wireframe exists, define the user problem, primary flow, required states, constraints, and unresolved decisions before creating polished screens.
4. List the frames or states needed and their dependencies. Capture the exact frame names as they are created.

Read [design-system-governance.md](references/design-system-governance.md) when the file has a design system or shared library. Read [prompt-and-review.md](references/prompt-and-review.md) before sending the first substantial Figma Agent prompt.

## Work in meaningful increments

Use one step per design decision, interaction pattern, or coherent state group. Do not reduce the work to one prompt per row, icon, or local frame.

- Establish one approved visual source before creating variants.
- Group variants that share the same settled pattern and can be reviewed together.
- Separate states when they introduce a new navigation pattern, hierarchy, menu, empty state, or data-truthfulness decision.
- Ask Figma Agent to stop after the named deliverable so the result can be inspected.
- Pause for the user when requested or when the next step depends on a real product decision. Otherwise continue after verification.

This balances two failure modes: a large prompt that produces many unchecked mistakes and tiny prompts that create unnecessary components or inconsistent local decisions.

## Protect the design system

Use this order of preference:

1. Existing variables, styles, and semantic tokens.
2. Existing generic primitives with the correct contract.
3. Feature-owned auto-layout frames and groups.
4. A new design-system primitive only when reuse is demonstrated.

Repeated structures inside one JusPrin feature, one screen family, or several states do not by themselves justify a design-system component. Keep feature rows, metadata blocks, local cards, summaries, and state-specific compositions local unless they satisfy the promotion test in the governance reference. Reuse must be demonstrated across independent JusPrin product surfaces, not across examples of the same feature.

When Figma Agent needs a missing item:

- First decide whether it is a generic primitive or feature composition.
- Add a generic primitive to the design system only when it has a stable contract and independent consumers.
- Keep a feature composition local even if it appears in several mockup states.
- Do not create specimen frames, variants, styles, or variables merely to make the current task easier.
- Do not detach or rewrite established library instances unless the requested design cannot be expressed through their intended properties.
- Do not add a Figma-only token or component value that has no corresponding repository role. Raise it as a design decision and, if approved, update the canonical token source as part of implementation work.

If Figma Agent creates accidental components or specimens, detach their feature instances if necessary, remove the new definitions, and verify that established library assets remain intact.

## Prompt Figma Agent precisely

Every creation prompt should name:

- the source frame or design to duplicate;
- the exact new or revised frame names;
- the current step's required state and behavior;
- elements that must remain unchanged;
- whether feature content should remain ordinary frames/groups;
- any existing primitives to reuse;
- content and ordering that must be exact;
- states or concepts that are explicitly out of scope;
- the stop condition and the selection Figma Agent should leave active.

Keep stable constraints short and consistent across prompts. Put most prompt detail into the current state delta. Attach the wireframe or reference when available; when it is not available, give Figma Agent a bounded problem statement and create low-cost structural alternatives before high-fidelity work.

For JusPrin high-fidelity frames, also require:

- one canonical appearance mode for each application screen; do not create a
  second light/dark screen frame solely to demonstrate theming;
- the other appearance mode must be deterministically derived by the design
  system from the same semantic token roles, component variants, geometry,
  content, and interaction state;
- light/dark comparisons belong in the design-system work needed to verify
  semantic mappings, not as duplicate application-screen deliverables;
- HarmonyOS Sans SC roles and the established functional SVG icon system;
- native desktop density and the documented radius, spacing, control-size, and typography roles;
- applicable hover, pressed, disabled, focus, success, warning, and error states;
- realistic long filenames, localized labels, dense data, empty states, and narrow-window behavior;
- no web-only glass, blur, oversized-control, or platform-specific-font treatment.

## Verify the canvas, not the agent's report

Figma Agent's completion summary is a claim, not verification. Inspect the result visually before moving on.

At minimum:

1. Inspect the whole frame for shell preservation, hierarchy, clipping, overlap, and balance.
2. Inspect the changed region at readable zoom.
3. Check exact text, counts, status labels, menu ordering, selection treatment, disclosure direction, conditional elements, and overlay placement.
4. Check that the frame uses intended variables and existing primitives.
5. Check the file for unintended components, variants, styles, variables, or specimen groups.
6. Confirm no unrelated approved frame changed.

When correction is needed, send a narrow correction prompt that names the affected frames and preserves every accepted detail. Reinspect the corrected result instead of relying on the summary.

After a frame passes, record its exact name and node URL. This prevents later handoff work from depending on memory or canvas search.

## Finish with a consistency pass

Before calling the design complete:

- compare shared structure across all states;
- confirm every required normal, selected, expanded, folded, menu, error, empty, and metadata state that applies;
- confirm conditional content appears only when relevant;
- remove abandoned explorations unless the user wants them retained as decision records;
- confirm the chosen alternative is clearly identified;
- confirm the design system contains only deliberate reusable additions.

For an implementation handoff, reference Figma frame names and node URLs for visual details. Document only behavior, data ownership, interaction rules, conditional logic, implementation boundaries, unresolved questions, and verification requirements that Figma does not communicate reliably.

Tie implementation notes back to JusPrin's ownership model and token source. Call out whether each surface is native, Agent-page, or retained OrcaSlicer UI, because that determines the implementation boundary and the allowed styling mechanism.
